opportunities.title: Ledger's $86M Hardware Implant: The Supply Chain Attack Everyone Said Couldn't Happen to Hardware Wallets
opportunities.why_now: Ledger just confirmed an unauthorized hardware implant with losses exceeding $86M, the exact 'cold storage is safe' assumption this channel exists to dismantle.
opportunities.angle: Technical breakdown of the implant vector + a 'how to verify your device wasn't tampered with' checklist, framed as 'we already knew this ends with hardware trust assumptions breaking'

opportunities.title: Coldcard's Own X Account Got Phished — The Day After Ledger's Implant Story
opportunities.why_now: A hardware wallet company's official account posting a phishing link, same week as the Ledger disaster, is a gift for a 'even the security vendors get compromised' thesis.
opportunities.angle: Short sharp X thread: timeline of the phishing post, what it means that the wallet makers can't secure their own distribution channels, call to never trust links from official accounts blindly

opportunities.title: The Ledger Reseller Hack Nobody Reads Past the Headline: How 'Southeast Asian Reseller' Becomes Your Attack Surface
opportunities.why_now: Ledger's own disclosure traces losses to a specific reseller, exposing the real vulnerability: the retail supply chain between manufacturer and buyer, not the chip.
opportunities.angle: Explainer/investigative angle on hardware wallet supply chain risk — where to buy, how to verify seals, why 'sealed box' isn't proof of anything anymore

opportunities.title: XRP Ledger Had a Decade-Old Bug That Could Print Billions of XRP From Nothing — And Nobody Noticed
opportunities.why_now: A silently patched, decade-old inflation bug in a top-10 chain's core ledger logic is exactly the kind of quiet near-catastrophe this channel's audience wants dissected after the fact.
opportunities.angle: Deep-dive postmortem: what the bug was, why it sat undetected for 10 years, and what it says about audit coverage on 'boring' established chains vs hot new L1s

opportunities.title: One Year After the $19B Flash Crash: Liquidity's Back, But Did Anyone Actually Fix Anything?
opportunities.why_now: The one-year anniversary retrospective is a natural hook for the channel's 'for people who already know how this ends' voice — liquidity metrics improved, but the structural fragility didn't.
opportunities.angle: Contrarian retrospective: use CoinDesk's own data (liquidity rebuilt, altcoins still fragile, volatility swings more frequent than 2018) to argue the market priced in recovery, not resilience
